title: Generative Adversarial Networks in Time Series: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Brophy, Eoin; Wang, Zhengwei; She, Qi; Ward, Tomás
tldr: This systematic review categorizes time series GANs into discrete and continuous variants, evaluating architectures, evaluation metrics, and privacy measures for synthetic temporal data generation.
problem_and_motivation: GANs have shown success in computer vision but face unique challenges when applied to time series data. There is no consensus on evaluation metrics for time series GANs, and training instability, mode collapse, and privacy risks remain significant barriers. The field lacks a comprehensive review specifically focused on time series applications.
approach: Systematic review following PRISMA guidelines across major databases.
Categorized GANs into discrete-variant (discrete time series) and continuous-variant (continuous time series).
Evaluated architectures including SeqGAN, Quant GAN, C-RNN-GAN, TimeGAN, and SigCWGAN.
Analyzed evaluation metrics: t-SNE, PCA, MMD, IS, FID for quality assessment.
Examined privacy measures including differential privacy and re-identification risks.
Identified applications in healthcare, finance, music generation, and sensor data.
findings: Discrete time series GANs struggle with zero gradient problem making generators untrainable via backpropagation alone.
SeqGAN addresses discrete generation using policy gradient and Monte Carlo search for reward estimation.
TimeGAN combines unsupervised GAN training with supervised autoregressive models for better temporal dynamics.
SigCWGAN uses Signature Wasserstein-1 metric to capture temporal dependencies efficiently.
Quant GAN applies temporal convolutional networks for financial time series with long-range dependencies.
No standardized benchmarking datasets exist for time series GAN evaluation.
Privacy risks include re-identification through linkage attacks on de-identified data.
Training stability challenges include vanishing gradients, mode collapse, and non-convergence.

key_equations.equation: GAN Value Function: $\min_G \max_D V(G,D) = \mathbb{E}_{x \sim p_{data}} [\log D(x)] + \mathbb{E}_{z \sim p_z} [\log(1-D(G(z)))]$
key_equations.explanation: Minimax game between generator and discriminator defining GAN training objective.
Loss function showing gradient vanishing when distributions have no overlap.

key_equations.equation: SeqGAN Policy Gradient: $\nabla_\theta J(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{Y \sim G_\theta} [\sum_{t=1}^T \nabla_\theta \log G_\theta(y_t|Y_{1:t-1}) \cdot R(Y)$
key_equations.explanation: Policy gradient update for discrete sequence generation using Monte Carlo rollouts.

key_equations.equation: TimeGAN Supervised Loss: $L_{supervised} = \mathbb{E}_{s,x_{1:T} \sim p} [\|h_t - g(h_{t-1}, z_t)\|_2]$
key_equations.explanation: Supervised loss ensuring temporal coherence in generated sequences.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic review provides the first comprehensive categorization of time series GANs into discrete and continuous variants. The taxonomy enables researchers to identify appropriate architectures for specific temporal data types. The analysis reveals that TimeGAN and SigCWGAN represent state-of-the-art approaches for continuous time series generation. The review highlights critical gaps including lack of standardized benchmarks, evaluation metrics, and privacy preservation frameworks. For financial applications, Quant GAN demonstrates potential for capturing long-range dependencies in market data.
directly_justifies: No standardized benchmarking datasets exist for time series GAN evaluation.

Quant GAN captures long-range dependencies in financial time series.
limits: Focuses on GANs specifically; other generative models like VAEs receive less attention.
Most reviewed works use relatively small datasets which may not scale.
No standardized evaluation metrics established for time series quality.
Privacy preservation techniques require further development for sensitive data.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all 14 topic domains revealed primary relevance to Domain 12 (Algorithms and Mathematical Foundations) and Domain 6 (Anomaly Detection). Topic 6.A (Anomaly Detection) received high relevance as GANs can generate synthetic data for anomaly detection. Topic 12.A (Clustering Methods) received high relevance for time series pattern recognition. Topic 12.B (Evaluation of Algorithmic Modules) received high relevance for comprehensive GAN evaluation. Topic 12.C (Model Explainability) received medium relevance for interpretability challenges. Domains 1-5, 7-11, 13-14 were considered and rejected as the paper focuses on generative models rather than Filipino demographics, financial behavioral profiles, expense categorization, predictive modeling in personal finance, budgeting strategies, mobile design, data privacy mechanisms, trust, savings/debt management, or synthetic data generation for finance.
